chunks: As for what Saʿd narrated from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan and al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from Aḥmad ibn Hilāl, from Muḥammad ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Hishām ibn Sālim, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, concerning:
A man performs wudu (ablution) and forgets to wash his private part after having urinated. He said: He should wash his private part and not repeat the salat (prayer).

So this report may be understood as referring to one who forgot to wash his private part with water, then remembered when water was unavailable. It is permissible for him to deem the salat (prayer) lawful by what had previously occurred of istinjaʾ with stones, and he is not required to repeat any prayer he performs afterward while the situation remains as we have described. Then when he finds water, it becomes obligatory for him to rewash the place, but he is not required to repeat the salat (prayer) that he performed when water was unavailable.

key_terms.بِالْأَحْجَارِ: with stones, i.e. dry cleansing materials
key_terms.عَدَمِ الْمَاءِ: the absence or unavailability of water
key_terms.يَغْسِلَ: to wash ritually in the context of removing impurity

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets to wash after urination and prays without water available, must the salat (prayer) be repeated?
ai.summary: This passage presents a legal ruling regarding one who forgets to wash the private part after urination before salat (prayer). It explains that the report is understood to apply to a case where water is unavailable, such that prior istinjaʾ with stones suffices for the prayer, and the prayer does not need to be repeated, though washing the area becomes obligatory once water is found.
